Cc: procurement@stalwarthealth.com

Subject: Subprocessor list + temporary cutover window for attestations

Hi Lauren / Kimberly,

Quick ask from our privacy and procurement teams: to finish our vendor review we need a minimal-scope subprocessor manifest (names, primary country of processing, and data path summary) and a proposed temporary cutover window for onboarding any transit processors (we may request an onshore fallback for a 48-hour validation). Can you also confirm whether any of the newly proposed subprocessors will have access to raw tenant data versus telemetry only?

We are aiming to close the DPA addendum this week; having the manifest and a proposed cutover schedule will let us finalize our internal SOC review. If you have a short change log or rotation plan for agent keys/tokens that would help too.

Thanks,
Daniel Price
Head of Vendor Risk – Stalwart Health
Daniel.Price@stalwarthealth.com

[attachment: example-risk-matrix.pdf (application/pdf) referenced]

Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it.

Quick notes:
- I'll own delivering the minimal-scope manifest (CSV) and a short narrative describing data paths.
- Kimberly will confirm which processors touch raw tenant payloads vs telemetry/metrics.
- Marissa will own the cutover windows and the rotation/rollback playbook.

Can you confirm the target timezone for the cutover window? You mentioned a 48-hour validation for onshore fallback — do you need us to schedule the primary cutover outside business hours in your region, or are overnight PT windows acceptable?

We plan to send a draft manifest and proposed windows by EOD PT today. If procurement needs a signed DPA annex simultaneously, flag that and we'll prioritize legal.

— Lauren

Folks — attaching the minimal-scope manifest and a preliminary temp-cutover schedule.

Summary (high level):
- Attachment: subprocessor_manifest.csv — columns: vendor_name, role, primary_country, data_types_accessed (raw_payload | telemetry | logs), legal_basis (DPA appendix ref), last_attestation_date.
- Of the items on this manifest, three processors may touch raw tenant payloads under our transit/transform path: EdgeCorridor (US), TokenBroker (US), and SecureSync (US). All others are telemetry/metrics only.
- Temporary cutover plan (attachment: temp_cutover_plan.xlsx): propose a 2-hour primary cutover window 02:00–04:00 PT (overnight) on July 7, 2026, with a 48-hour onshore fallback standby window the following day for validation if Stalwart requests onshore processing. The standby would not be enabled unless we receive a signed onshore addendum; it's a configured fallback rather than an active switch.
- Rotation/rollback notes: we will rotate agent API keys immediately prior to cutover, with a TTL-based staged rollout (stage 1: 10% traffic, stage 2: 50% traffic, stage 3: 100%) and automatic rollback on error threshold (>1.5% 5xx for 5 minutes).

Attachments included as stubs below — please tell me if you need a redacted view.

Attachments:
- subprocessor_manifest.csv (text/csv)
- temp_cutover_plan.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Drive draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-Cutover-Docs (internal edit)

—Kimberly

Kimberly / Lauren — this is great, thanks for the fast turnaround. A few follow-ups from our privacy team after reviewing the manifest:

1) Can you provide a redacted CSV that omits internal contact emails but preserves vendor names and country processing?
2) For the three processors that may touch raw payloads, please confirm what data minimization controls are in place (e.g., encryption at rest/in transit, field redaction, TTL of stored artifacts).
3) We need a DocuSign link for the onshore fallback DPA annex if you can generate one; procurement would like to sign and return within 24 hours to enable the standby fallback.

If you can get the redacted manifest and a short control checklist by EOD our side will begin the internal sign-off. After sign-off we'll confirm whether we want the standby enabled on July 8 as proposed.

Appreciate it — Daniel
